verdict.rationale: monday.com documents its own event-triggered behavior. Users can build agents where they 'set the rules', and those agents fire on events such as being messaged, assigned an item, or mentioned. Integrations can also 'trigger automations', and developers can listen for real-time events like create_item and change_column_value and run workflows when data changes. However, the evidence never describes a general user-facing rule builder (when event X happens, do action Y) with documented triggers, conditions and actions. Much of the event coverage is developer-level subscription rather than end-user rules. Community comments in the pack do not address automation and were ignored. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a no-code event→action rule builder, a catalog of available triggers/conditions/actions, independent or hands-on corroboration that event rules work.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Build agents for your exact needs. Define the goal, set the rules, watch the results.
Fire when an agent is messaged, assigned an item, or mentioned in an update.
Enable 2-way sync between monday products and any platform you work with to trigger automations, eliminate manual work, and keep your business in motion.
Listen for real-time events and run your workflow the moment data changes.
